case_number: 2024 INSC 1026; CIVIL APPEAL NO. 14808 OF 2024 (Arising out of SLP (C)No. 4293 of 2021)

parties.respondent: The State Of Madhya Pradesh & Anr.

summary: Stamp duty chargeability on compromise decree; no new title creation versus pre-existing possession; civil suit for declaration/injunction followed by consent decree; mutation application post-decree; Collector of Stamps invoked Section 33, Indian Stamp Act 1899; High Court upheld duty under Article 22A; Registration Act s.17(2)(vi) exemption for court orders; factual distinction from Bhoop Singh (collusive decree) and Siddhulal cases; Yusuf precedent binding where decree conveys pre-existing right; no evidence of collusion; stamp duty not payable when no new right created.
legal_provisions_cited: Indian Stamp Act, 1899 s.3, s.33, Article 22A, Schedule I
final_judgment: Appeal allowed; Collector of Stamps order, Board of Revenue affirmation, and High Court judgment set aside; stamp duty liability extinguished.
